cases.given: A repository already has an authoritative project plan and asks for an additional implementation outcome.
expect: Preserve the existing plan as the only durable planning owner.
Apply compatible planning-quality guardrails without creating a second plan, journal, or database.
Treat any runtime plan as a disposable view rather than canonical state.

cases.given: An active Plan has one current in-progress Work Item plus several todo and done Work Items.
expect: Require at most one in-progress Work Item and require it to equal current_item.
Preserve the other Work Items when they represent real outcome boundaries.
Do not interpret the concurrency limit as a one-Work-Item total limit.

cases.given: A small calculator behavior is already tracked in one Work Item and needs implementation plus focused verification.
expect: Keep one behavior-complete Work Item for the observable result.
Keep implementation order in optional Steps.
Keep testing in Acceptance or Evidence unless it is an independently requested deliverable.

cases.given: A structural change has schema, compatibility, consumer-update, and rollout outcomes that can be blocked or resumed independently.
expect: Split independently resumable outcomes into separate Work Items.
Express genuine boundary order with dependencies and subordinate implementation order with Steps.
Keep all outcomes in the repository's one canonical Plan.

cases.given: Implementation has been written, but its acceptance checks have not been observed.
expect: Keep the Work Item non-terminal and do not invent Evidence.
Advance Next action to the first unobserved test, build, browser check, review, or evaluator-owned verification.
Mark the Work Item done only after observing its Acceptance result and recording concise evidence.

cases.given: A repository with no planning profile requests one small reversible change and has no durable planning requirement.
expect: Do not initialize a Plan profile or read absent canonical files.
Implement and validate the contained change directly.
Use a lightweight runtime plan only when the host independently requires one, without making it canonical.
